text: Kitten lethargic after deworming My bf and I picked a kitty up off the street on Sunday took her to her first vet appt Thursday. Vet estimated her to be about 4 weeks. She was given dewormer at the vet and told me to come back in 2 weeks for her first round of shots. The day of her deworming, she ate fine, she played a little bit(definitely less than usual) and she seemed a little tired. It didn’t seem entirely out of the ordinary. Friday morning she ate her breakfast fine and seemed about the same as Thursday afternoon/night— not quite as playful but still pretty active. She wasn’t having diarrhea so I wasn’t sure if it just took a couple days to take effect? I just kept my eye on her until I left for work. However, Friday night she threw up one time and had some questionable looking stool, I assumed she was beginning to pass them. She did not play much at all, she seemed very sleepy. When she normally would play, she would just follow us around and whine/meow, it was starting to seem like she didn’t feel good. This morning, she had very loose stool and only wants to lie down. She will still follow us around but not too much, now will just lie down and go to sleep if we aren’t in the room with her. She hasn’t thrown up at all besides that one time. I’ve seen a lot of stuff about dewormer killing kittens and I’m a little worried. At what point do I stop scraping it up to the dewormer just doing what it’s supposed to be doing? I don’t want to make the judgement to call the vet too late.

text: Baby Cat rescued from elevator shaft I heard her when I was going down the elevator ,and since our stupid elevator doesn’t show numbers, I didn’t know which exact floor she was on. When her voice got louder, I guessed she was around the 4th floor. I went up stairs and kept hearing her. I opened the door on the 2nd floor to see if she’d react. I heard her voice, looked up, and finally saw her peeking at me. I waited there and kept the elevator door open just in case, because when it closes, the distance between the door and the wall is like 1–2 cm. When a woman came, I asked her to help me keep the elevator door open. I was too short to reach her, so the woman suggested I wait while she brought a chair. I got up and quickly got her out, headfirst. Her claws were trying to cling to the sides, so I tried to remove them one by one. Then I took her home, fed her some softened cat kibble, chicken, and a quail egg, and she played a little and met my 6-year-old cat. I wanted to keep her, but sadly, my family didn’t want me to.( I think they gave her to the neighbor) I can’t imagine how terrified she must have been in that cold, dark place, hearing the loud elevator. I keep wondering how long she was there, but I’m glad she wasn’t hurt.

text: My cat was misgendered This sweet baby came onto my porch demanding food roughly 2 months ago. We got her to the vet for checks and vaccines multiple times, did bloodwork, checked body temperature, the works. I asked the vet if my cat is a girl or a boy, told the vet that the cat is a stray and I don’t know its background. I got reassured that she’s a girl, so we finally scheduled her to get a spay. We got her inside for the night, fasted her, prepared everything carefully for our little princess, brought her in and waited anxiously at home for the call to go collect her. The surgeon personally called me, asked for my name, confirmed that she’s my cat, told me that something happened, it sometimes happens and he’s sorry. I got so anxious I was sweating and trembling thinking that my cat didn’t make it, but I got told that my little princess is in fact a prince. Turns out he was neutered as a kitten and has a very small wee wee. I am still recovering after 2 days, and my poor little guy got a full abdominal surgery he didn’t need and I feel so guilty. I had my suspicions and looked at his face multiple times thinking he looks like a boy, but ultimately trusted the vet. He doesn’t like it inside and cries so much for the outdoors life and he has to be kept prisoner because of a surgery he didn’t need. Beyond shock, I feel just so sad for him. I feel so guilt. Let this be your sign to double check if you have doubts and listen to your gut. TL;DR: The stray cat that landed on my porch was pronounced female by the vet, took her for a spay, the abdominal surgery revealed he’s in fact a neutered male.

text: Be kind I was out enjoying my morning car solo date when I noticed this cute little cat talking to me. 😂i tried getting closer, but he wasn’t interested in being captured and walked away. I went upstairs, grabbed some cat food, and came back down, but he was nowhere to be found. I figured I’d just keep the food in my car and continue enjoying my day. Y’ALL. 😭😭😭 This little baby came BACK and jumped onto my car hood!! I immediately put the plate of food out the window, and he started eating. I got to sit there and watch him have his meal, then I gently moved the food to the ground when he hopped down so he could keep eating. ❤️ I tried getting closer again, but he walked away, so I let him be. I just wanted to make sure he got something to eat. The timing of this whole encounter was so beautiful to me. I’ve been in this season of choosing myself, building better routines, protecting my peace, and learning that I can still be a nurturing, giving person without giving myself away in the process, and today, I got to give simply because I could. No expectations. No strings attached. Just a hungry little baby who needed a meal. I don’t know if he’ll come back, if he has a home, or what his story is, but I genuinely hope he has a safe journey and finds kindness along the way. 🥹🐾 I went out for a solo car date and got an unexpected little reminder of something meaningful to me: I can keep my heart soft without abandoning myself. I can give when I have something to give and still keep my own peace. What a gift to give. ❤️ The gift that keeps on giving. Please be safe out there, little baby. I hope life is kind to you. 🐈💕
